main_text.p: ter temporibus æqualibus super centro eccentrico-rum priorum.

Nominatur itaque orbis super quo est centrum epicycli, eccentricus deferens centrum epicycli: orbis autem primus, super cuius centro mouetur centrum epicycli æqualiter, dicitur eccentricus æquans curfum.

Vnaquæque autem superficies horum orbium eccentricorum in sex planetis, secat superficiem zodiaci in duo hemicyclia, iuxta duo opposita loca: & declinat ab ea in duabus partibus versus septentrionem & meridiem: & spacium quod ab utraque sectione intercipitur appellatur draco: punctum a quo incipit orbis planetæ declinare ab orbe signorum ad septentrionem, vocatur caput draconis, sine geuzohar, & punctum oppositum dicitur cauda draconis.

In luna superficies epicycli est inseparabilis a superficie eccentrici, ut non declinet ab ea: quapropter inest ei in latitudine diuersitas una, propter declinationem eccentrici eius ab orbe signorum.

Quinque vero reliquorum planetarum epicycli declinant ab eccentricis duplicirter: quare contingunt vnicuique eorum diuersitates duæ, quarum una est propter declinationem eccentrici a signifero, altera accidit propter declinationem epicycli ab eccentrico. Atqhæ sunt hypothesis a sapientibus tradita de sphæris cælestibus.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Atqhæ" in the last line is probably "Atqui hæ" (line-end, the "qui" is abbreviated or badly printed); "geuzohar" is printed as such (Hebrew transliteration, Latin letters, kept as printed); "duplicirter" and "eccentricis" kept as printed; "sex planetis" read as printed (the scan shows "sex" with long s, transcribed as s). The catchword and the signature at the foot read "E iiij" on the scan, with the last j partly faint.
